summary: Distinguish a present field from a missing field.
documentation: Object.hasOwn reports whether a property belongs directly to an object, even if its value is null, false or zero. It ignores inherited properties and does not call an object’s potentially overwritten hasOwnProperty method.
inputs: An object and a property key.
returns: A Boolean indicating direct property ownership.
caution: Presence and truthiness answer different questions. Do not reject a present zero or null value merely because it is falsey.
scenarios: Distinguish an omitted configuration option from an explicitly disabled one.
Validate whether an imported record supplied a required field.
Detect whether a patch intentionally clears a saved value.
title: Check whether a discount was supplied
problem: Input is a JSON object. Return true when it has its own discount property, even if that value is null, false or 0. Return false when the property is absent.
goal: Use Object.hasOwn() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Test ownership rather than reading the value as a Boolean.
